1: The aged vizier Ptahhotep, when his strength failed, asked leave of the king to teach his son. And the king said: Teach him the words of the past, for the speech of the ancients is a ladder, and he who climbs by it rises above his years. And this is the first wisdom: that the young are not ashamed to learn, nor the old to teach.

Do not be arrogant because of your knowledge; take counsel with the ignorant as with the wise. The limits of art are not reached, and no artist is master of perfection. Good speech is more hidden than the emerald, yet it may be found among the handmaids at the millstones.

If you are a man of note, sitting at the table of one greater than you, take what is set before you, and look only at what is before you — do not look at what is before him. He who stares is one who fails; he who is at ease is the guest of the house.
2: Do not let your heart be hasty; restraint is life. He who is ruled by his anger is ruled by a servant, and the servant has no love for him. Calm your heart, and the day will calm with it, for the day takes its temper from the hearts of those who walk in it.

Love your wife with all your heart: fill her belly, clothe her back, and anoint her limbs with oil. Make her glad while she lives with you — for she is a field that brings forth blessing, and her gladness is the harvest.

If you hear a man speak evil of another, do not carry the word; and if you carry the word, it will carry you. The mouth that is a road for slander becomes a road for ruin, and no one builds on a road of ruin.
3: Wealth, like a stone in the stream, is worn smooth by the water; and the water is time, and the time is not yours. What endures is the heart that has loved, and the mouth that has spoken truth, and the hand that has given — these are the three stones the water cannot move.

As for him who hears these words and does them, his house shall be established and his name shall be good. He shall speak as the ancients spoke, and his son shall speak after him, and the words shall be a boat that carries them all across the river that no one crosses twice.

See, I have spent my years and my months in the house of the king, and I have seen what the heart of man is. And the heart of man, when it is turned toward truth, is the throne of God; and when it is turned away, it is a boat with no oars, in a river with no banks. Choose the throne.
